## Problem
A misleading error code is a significant failure mode: it causes LLM/agent consumers to make erroneous assumptions and act on a wrong diagnosis (e.g. "the AI provider is down" when the real fault is bad input or a missing asset). Recent bugs are all instances of ONE systemic pattern: the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` fallthrough in the `error_code_for` classifier mislabels non-availability failures.

## Goal
Systematically audit EVERY error-code / classification surface so each returned code accurately and specifically describes the actual condition, and no failure degrades to a misleading catch-all.

## Reconciled taxonomy (RESOLVED — supersedes the pre-dbca brief)
Epic dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d has since LANDED (closed; commits ae4f6c1a, f854924b) and already reclassified the workflow caller-input family with FINER, more descriptive codes than a broad `command_failed`. Per the operator descriptiveness bar a finer accurate code is strictly better, so dbca's answer is preserved, not competed with. The authoritative target for this epic is therefore:
- `LLMUnavailableError` / `LLMConfigError` -> `llm_unavailable` (genuine availability faults only).
- `LLMRunnerError` subtree (`LLMBudgetExhaustedError`, `ContextWindowExceededError`, `LLMInputRejectedError`, `RunawayToolLoopError`, `StructuredOutputError`/`UnretryableOutputError`/`CompletionRecoveryError`) -> `command_failed` (the residual mislabel this epic fixes).
- dbca workflow caller-input subtree (`WorkflowNotFoundError` -> `not_found`; `WorkflowParseError`/`WorkflowValidationError`/`WorkflowVersionError`/`WorkflowUnknownStepError` -> `invalid_input`) -> PRESERVED UNTOUCHED.
- bare `WorkflowError` base + bare `LLMError` -> `llm_unavailable` (dbca's pinned catch-all; the still-open escalated ticket 551b owns any future change to the bare-base editor/missing-bundle code — this epic does NOT pre-decide it).
Discriminate by exception TYPE, not by phase. Do NOT revert dbca. Do NOT invent new fine-grained error codes beyond what a consumer demonstrably needs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `error_code_for` (src/rebar/_errors.py) routes the `LLMRunnerError` subtree to `command_failed` while keeping `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMConfigError` -> `llm_unavailable`, and leaves dbca's workflow caller-input taxonomy (`not_found`/`invalid_input`) and the bare `WorkflowError`/`LLMError` catch-all (`llm_unavailable`) untouched (child f75f-5509-10c0-4430).
- [x] `_structured_llm_failure` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py) derives its top-level `error` field via `error_code_for(exc)` instead of hardcoding `llm_unavailable`, across all 4 MCP gate tools, so both dbca's finer codes and the LLMRunnerError routing apply uniformly (child fbc0-ee15-9d69-49ae).
- [x] The `render_workflow` MCP tool surfaces the `WorkflowError` caller-input family as `not_found`/`invalid_input` (NOT `llm_unavailable`) — already proven observably by the landed dbca contract tests (tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py). 7d47-2131-42bd-4832 is therefore closed as SUPERSEDED by dbca; no `command_failed` is re-asserted for that family.
- [x] `pinned_ticket_read_failed` is registered in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (child 0aee-a70d-045b-48a1).
- [x] The gate-degrade `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean is True only for genuine `LLMUnavailableError` outages; `LLMInputRejectedError` instead sets a distinct `input_rejected` signal (via a shared `failure.degrade_cause_flags` helper applied in BOTH degrade builders — `gate_dispatch.py` and `plan_review_recovery.py`), and the three readers (`plan_review/drift_floor.py`, `plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `review_bot/adapter.py`) are updated to read it. No broad `degraded` category (child 5f96-25aa-af9d-4f57).
- [x] A prevention guardrail lands: an exhaustive `exception -> code` contract test over the `LLMError` subclass tree asserting the RECONCILED taxonomy above (availability -> `llm_unavailable`; `LLMRunnerError` subtree -> `command_failed`; dbca workflow subtree -> `not_found`/`invalid_input`; bare bases -> `llm_unavailable`), plus a vocabulary-closure test asserting every code any producer can emit is in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (pins 0aee).
- [x] [non-codebase] Every change lands via Gerrit with `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`, carries a `rebar-ticket` trailer + DCO sign-off, and children are closed bottom-up.
  provenance: environment=gerrit@rebar.solutions.navateam.com + github-actions-ci; principal=rebar review-bot (LLM-Review) and CI Verified bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit changes 2413/2415 merged to main and 2416/2418/2419 each carry Verified +1 and LLM-Review +1 (confirmed via live Gerrit REST /detail), every commit carries a rebar-ticket trailer + DCO Signed-off-by, and children f75f/fbc0/7d47/0aee/5f96 were closed bottom-up before this epic close.

## Scope (surfaces enumerated by the audit)
- `error_code_for` mapping (`src/rebar/_errors.py`) — the residual blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` branch 7 (branch 6 workflow classification already handled by dbca).
- `_structured_llm_failure` (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) across the 4 MCP gate tools.
- The gate-degrade `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean (`gate_dispatch.py` + `plan_review_recovery.py`) and its three readers.
- Top-level `_errors.py` `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` vocabulary contract.

## Constraints
Remediation lands via Gerrit per AGENTS.md. No --force. Gates run unbounded. dbca (landed) is preserved, not reverted. 551b remains OPEN and owns the bare-`WorkflowError`-base editor/missing-bundle decision — this epic explicitly does not resolve it.
